newsitem.title: FRANCE: Asterix leaves retirement, travels to Atlantis.
newsitem.headline: Asterix leaves retirement, travels to Atlantis.

text.p: Asterix the irrepressible Gaul comes out of retirement on Thursday for a comic strip trip to the legendary lost continent of Atlantis to rescue his dim-witted friend Obelix from Roman kidnappers.

The book, with a record print run of eight million copies in 15 languages, goes on sale across Europe after being transported by truck and ship in a secret operation of which Asterix's Roman opponents would have been proud.
"Asterix and Obelix All at Sea" is the first book in the French cartoon series since 1991 and the 30th in a series that has sold 280 million copies worldwide with its knockabout, slapstick humour.
The books, about a tiny village resisting the Roman invasion of Gaul in 50 BC with the help of a magic strength-giving potion, have been translated into 78 languages.
In the new book, the rotund and slow-minded Obelix turns to stone and then reverts to a tiny childhood size after wrongly overdosing on the magic potion.

Mini-Obelix is seized and held hostage on Julius Caesar's galley. The Gauls set off to rescue him in an adventure to Atlantis, proving Plato was wrong to have said in the fourth century BC that the island had sunk beneath the waves.

Asterix's creator, Albert Uderzo, said he regretted saying in 1994 that the Gallic freedom fighters had retired for good. He said the announcement came in a moment of fatigue after losing a lawsuit against a former publisher.
"I wanted to start again because I don't feel old enough to stop work," Uderzo told Reuters at the Parc Asterix theme park north of Paris, a rival to Disneyland Paris.
Uderzo, who is colour-blind, was swamped by excited children as he posed shyly beside Asterix and a nodding Obelix on a bridge in the miniature Asterix village.
He declined to predict whether the book would be the runaway success needed to match the giant print run. "I'm happy to have made it, I hope readers will be happy to read it," he said.

Others are sure the book is a winner. "I think it's a brilliant book with many good jokes, lovely characters and a great many old friends," said Anthea Bell, who has helped to translate all the Asterix books.

The new characters include a high priest, Absolutlifabulous. U.S. actor Kirk Douglas makes a special guest appearance as a Greek slave, "Spartakis", a play of his name as the lead in the Hollywood movie "Spartacus".
The book is the sixth Uderzo has penned alone since the death of writer Rene Goscinny.

Some readers say the wit and plots have lost some of their sparkle since Uderzo took on both the drawing and the writing. But the latest books far outsold the early adventures, a fact Uderzo puts down to better marketing.
Asterix first appeared in the magazine Pilote in 1959. Fans attribute the books' success to their portrayal of a band of amiable underdogs fighting repression.
